writeup.headline: Assurant rates Buy on strong cash generation, an absolutely low P/FCF and solid price momentum.
writeup.thesis: Assurant scores 68, a Buy, carried mainly by valuation (80), quality (79) and trend (77). In absolute terms the shares look inexpensive, at 8.5x free cash flow and 1.0x sales, with an FCF yield 6.8 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock sits near the middle of its own history (the multiples disagree: P/S expensive, P/FCF cheap). Quality is supported by a 12.3% FCF margin, low stock-based pay at 0.7% of revenue and the diluted share count down 2.5% year on year. Growth is middling at 50, with TTM revenue growth of 9.4% but growth slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter, and news risk is neutral at 50; the balance sheet factor could not be scored.
key_risks: Revenue growth slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter; further deceleration would weigh on the growth score.
Catastrophe losses can hit results, since the raised 2026 outlook excludes reportable catastrophes.
Q3 results on November 3, 2026 could disappoint after the August outlook raise.
P/S is more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends, so a slip in cash flow would leave less valuation support.
Analyst views are mixed, including a Morgan Stanley target cut and a downgrade to Hold from Wall Street Zen.
what_would_change: A drop of 4 points would move the rating to Hold, for example if momentum fades or growth slows further.
Gaining 12 points would reach Strong Buy, which would likely need re-accelerating revenue growth alongside positive news such as another outlook raise.
A weaker Q3 or guidance cut on November 3 could lower the news risk and growth scores.
A sharp rise in the share price without matching cash flow growth would reduce the valuation score.
